requirements.evidence: All contract pieces are present: pairing command/action (app/Console/Commands/TotemPairingCode.php:11-40, app/Actions/OpenTotemPairing.php:21-42), HS256 claims (app/Support/TotemToken.php:33-41), auth middleware (app/Http/Middleware/AuthenticateTotem.php:24-57), the three endpoints and error codes (app/Http/Controllers/Api/TotemController.php:22-133), CORS (config/cors.php:16-33), docs and env changes. The exception is the throttling: the 10/min pair and 30/min ticket declarations at routes/api.php:10 and routes/api.php:21 share one Laravel counter, so one required edge case is wrong.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes go through App\Actions\OpenTotemPairing and App\Actions\PairTotem; migrations are generated-style with reversible down() (database/migrations/2026_10_29_055917_create_totems_table.php:18-25); fillable/hidden are explicit (app/Models/Totem.php:14, app/Models/TotemPreset.php:16-25); docs, CHANGELOG and phpunit.xml are updated. Minor deviations: composer.json:13 adds firebase/php-jwt with no visible composer.lock update, and TotemAuthController.php:25 hand-rolls the one-field validation instead of the project's inline $request->validate pattern (though the bespoke 400 body explains it).

security.evidence: JWT algorithm is pinned to HS256 and the HMAC key must be at least 32 chars (app/Support/TotemToken.php:22,33-41,69-77); malformed/forged/expired/unsigned tokens return null (TotemToken.php:49-57); every call re-loads an active totem and preset and verifies entity agreement (AuthenticateTotem.php:33-43); scope is intersected with the preset's current queues (AuthenticateTotem.php:47-52); login_code is hidden and never logged (TotemPreset.php:25, TotemAuthController.php:26-50); CORS is origin-restricted with credentials disabled (config/cors.php:20-24,33); no client-supplied IDs or ownership are trusted.

tests.evidence: Feature tests cover pairing success/failure/consume-once, the code-format matrix, the common 401, expired/forged/unsigned tokens, missing or inactive totem/preset/entity, last_seen_at, scope intersection, queues, priorities, ticket issuance, 403/404/422 paths, CORS and throttles; unit tests cover JWT claims/TTL/secret and the command/model tests cover pairing and relations. Gap: the throttle tests run each route in isolation (tests/Feature/Totem/TotemAuthTest.php:84, tests/Feature/Totem/TotemTicketTest.php:118), so the shared counter between the routes is untested.

simplicity.evidence: Reuses App\Actions\IssueTicket with channel totem (app/Http/Controllers/Api/TotemController.php:110-113), uses one TotemPriority enum for both the priorities response and validation, and adds no service/repository layer. Small duplication remains: the preset queue-id extraction is repeated in app/Actions/PairTotem.php:44 and app/Http/Middleware/AuthenticateTotem.php:47, and the queue payload shaping is repeated in TotemController.

readability.evidence: Small, named methods with useful docblocks (TotemToken, PairTotem, OpenTotemPairing, AuthenticateTotem); clear error helpers forbidden()/inactiveQueue(); resolveQueue documents its resolution order (app/Http/Controllers/Api/TotemController.php:136-145); style matches sibling app files; no debug output or dead code.

scope.evidence: Every file in the diff serves the totem BFF: models, migrations, factories, actions, command, middleware, controllers, routes, config, env, tests and the required docs. The extra business-rules/architecture/database-schema/ops/changelog edits are the project's docs-freshness requirement; no unrelated refactors or features.

issues.explanation: Laravel's unnamed throttle key is derived from the route domain and client IP only, so the pairing throttle:10,1 and ticket throttle:30,1 share a single counter (ten ticket requests in a minute make the next pairing request return 429, and pairing attempts consume the ticket budget); use named rate limiters or distinct throttle prefixes so the 10/min and 30/min limits stay independent as the task requires.

firebase/php-jwt is added to require but no composer.lock change is included; if the lock is tracked (the normal Laravel setup), composer install will not install the package and JWT issuance/validation will fail with Class "Firebase\JWT\JWT" not found, so commit the lock update in the same change.

The throttle tests exercise each route in isolation, so they do not catch the shared counter; add a mixed test (for example ten pairing attempts followed by a valid ticket request) once the limits are separated.
The same preset queue-id pluck/map/all block is duplicated; a TotemPreset::queueIds() helper would keep the scope definition in one place.

review.summary: Implements the totem BFF end-to-end: pairing command and action, HS256 JWT, totem.auth middleware with scope intersection, the three endpoints, CORS, docs and a broad Pest suite. The main defect is that both throttle declarations use Laravel's unnamed per-IP key, so the 10/min pairing and 30/min ticket budgets share one counter and can 429 each other; the diff also adds firebase/php-jwt without a visible composer.lock update. Those need to be addressed before merging, though the rest of the implementation is clean and well tested.
